newsitem.title: USA: Stocks slump after one-day bounce fizzles. [CORRECTED 00:05 GMT 3/4]
newsitem.headline: Stocks slump after one-day bounce fizzles. [CORRECTED 00:05 GMT 3/4]

text.p: The stock market slumped again Wednesday after a one-day bounce due to fears that rising interest rates could further pressure stocks.
The Dow Jones industrial average lost 94.04 points to end at 6,517.01. The Nasdaq Composite index fell 15.93 points to 1,201.00.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 1,710 to 816 on active volume of 478 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"Everybody has their horns pulled in," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers.
The blue-chip Dow index was sent reeling Thursday and Monday, posting back-to-back losses that totalled nearly 300 points. That was followed by a 28-point rise on Tuesday.
But investors were not in a buying mood, and Wednesday's downturn put the Dow 8 percent below its record closing high of 7,085.16 set March 11.
The Nasdaq index, which is studded with high-technology stocks, has shed 13.5 percent since its Jan. 22 high of 1,388.06.
The stock market has been sliding since the Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates last week in an effort to keep the economy from over-heating.

The possibility of additional rate hikes, amid signs the economy was still growing at a steady clip, has led to concerns on Wall Street that rate hikes would cool off the economy and bring a slowdown in corporate profit growth.
A string of economic data showing a resilient economy has fanned fears that last week's hike in short term interest rates would only be the first in a series of increases.
Stocks also were dogged by a jump in the yield for the key 30-year Treasury bond to 7 percent has led many investors to shift to bonds, avoiding the volatile stock market.
In the bond market, the 30-year bond rose 1/32, or 31 cents on a $1,000 bond, and its yield fell to 7.07 percent from Tuesday's close of 7.08 percent.
Analysts said Friday's employment report for March will be critical for the near-term direction in bonds and stocks.
Some traders said the corporate earnings reporting season, which starts next week, could stem the downturn in stocks.
But Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities, said the stronger dollar may hurt the results of multinational corporations.
"It's not over yet by any means," she said of the sell-off.

Craig Callahan, chief investment officer at Meridian Investment Management, said that given the Fed rate hike, the Dow would need to drop another 5 to 7 percent before stocks became attractively valued, barring further rate rises.

Energy companies, including oil drilling and services were among the hardest hit amid a drop in crude oil prices. Schlumberger Ltd. sank 3-3/8 to 106-5/8, Falcon Drilling Co. shed 1-5/8 to 34-1/2 and Diamond Offshore Drilling Inc. eased 2-1/8 to 65-3/8.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil for May (corrects from April) delivery fell 81 cents to $19.47 a barrel.
H&R Block Inc., which owns about 80 percent of online service CompuServe Corp., said the two companies were in talks with a third party regarding a possible business combination involving CompuServe.

The statement came amid rumours that industry leader American Online Inc. was negotiating to buy its rival. CompuServe finished up 1-5/8 to 12-5/8. American Online fell 1-1/8 to 44-5/8 and H&R Block was unchanged at 30-5/8.
Software maker FileNet Corp. tumbled 4-7/8 to 11 after saying it would report a loss in its first quarter due to weak sales.

The stock of retail pharmacy chain ShopKo Stores Inc. rose 1-1/4 to 16-1/2 on expectations that its major stockholder would be able to find a new deal to replace the $1 billion merger with Phar-Mor Inc. The companies said their merger was called off due to "continuing uncertainties." Phar-Mor rose 3/8 to 5-3/8.
Project Software & Development Inc. sank 15-15/16 to 15-5/16 after the company said its second quarter earnings would fall below last year's level.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 9.53 points to 750.11. The American Stock Exchange index lost 5.08 to 561.19.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 4.43 to 395.37. The average share was down 46 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,140.673 down 81.744 or 1.13 percent.
